selected.title: The ride and the recall
selected.texas_link: Waymo's robotaxi service in San Antonio opened to anyone with the app on October 14th, 2026, airport included, and a federal recall about flooded roads still lists its remedy as under development. The film draws a generic car, a curb and a lane as illustration and shows no real address.

movement.action: opened its San Antonio robotaxi service to anyone with the app, including the airport
movement.object: driverless ride hailing in San Antonio

selected.why_today: The service opened to everyone on October 14th, 2026, and the federal recall record read on October 19th lists the flood remedy as currently under development.
selected.consequence: More people, including airport travelers, can now hail a driverless car in San Antonio while the recall's remedy for driving into standing water is listed as currently under development.
selected.application_change: Driverless ride hailing in San Antonio moves from invited riders to anyone with the app, with the airport included.
selected.counter_image: The record doesn't say what the interim weather limits are or whether they apply now. The recall notice itself was not retrieved and the film states no cause of the April events.
selected.earned_take: The ride is open to everyone, and the federal record lists the flood remedy as currently under development.

agency.next_step: NHTSA's record lists the remedy as currently under development and names no date for it.
agency.who_can_act: Waymo sets its own service rules and NHTSA holds the recall record. Riders can choose whether to ride, and the public can read the recall record.

filmability.viewer_question: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a driverless Waymo to the airport. What does the federal record say about the flood problem its recall covers?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated white robotaxi pulls up at an airport curb in San Antonio and a phone shows a ride hail, disclosed as Illustration. It carries no brand mark.
filmability.mechanism: Input: a road with standing water across it. Transformation, as the recall sentence words it: the software may let the car slow and then drive into the water on a higher speed road. Result: the federal record lists the remedy as under development, with an interim step of tighter weather limits and updated maps by April 20th. Limit: the record doesn't say what the limits are or whether they apply now.
filmability.human_consequence: People who can now hail a ride in San Antonio, including airport travelers, and other road users. The April cars were unoccupied and no one was injured. No rider is named and no outcome for any person is claimed.
filmability.source_limit: The record gives the mechanism in one sentence with no cause, speed or depth. The interim weather limits are not defined and their current status isn't confirmed. Waymo's October 14th post doesn't mention flooding. The recall notice itself was not retrieved. No footage of the April events was used.
three_key_images: An illustrated robotaxi at an airport curb while a phone shows a ride request
An illustrated lane with standing water across it and the car slowing then rolling into it, labelled illustration of the recall wording, with no crash drawn
The recall record card reading remedy currently under development beside a tag reading interim limits by April 20th

action_support.pictured_action: An illustrated robotaxi pulls up at an airport curb and a phone shows the ride request.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory illustration of the October 14th opening. It shows no real airport, no real rider and no brand mark.
action_support.relationship: Waymo's own post says anyone in San Antonio can download the app and hail a fully autonomous ride, including to the San Antonio International Airport.

action_support.pictured_action: An illustrated car slows and then rolls into standing water across a higher speed lane, with the recall sentence beside it and no crash drawn.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory illustration of the federal recall wording. It shows no real road, no measured speed or depth and not the April event.
action_support.relationship: The federal recall record says the software may allow the vehicle to slow and then drive into standing water on higher speed roadways.

action_support.pictured_action: A recall record card reads remedy currently under development beside an interim limits tag dated April 20th and an open airport curb.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of the recall record's status fields. It shows no rider and no outcome for any person.
action_support.relationship: The federal recall record lists the remedy as under development and says the interim update reached all affected vehicles by April 20th, 2026.
